messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: scale vs scale.model
parts:
Hi,

I have just noticed the 'scale' option in the f() function. Is iid somewhat related to 'scale.model'? I have not been able to find any documentation about 'scale'.

Best,

Virgilio

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] scale vs scale.model
parts:
its defined in the relevant doc, here for the iid model

inla.doc("^iid$")

it is a fixed scaling of the precision, which defaults to 1.

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] scale vs scale.model
parts:
Hi,

Thanks for clarifying this! Is 'scale' only available in the 'iid' model? Also, if scale is used (assumed it is available for other models) this will also change the scale of the distribution of the hyperparameter tau, right? So, although 'scale.model' is thought for intrinsic models, both options will have an impact on the distribution of tau.

Best,

Virgilio

El lun., 4 mar. 2019 a las 11:17, Helpdesk (<he...@r-inla.org>) escribió:
scale.model is related to improper/intrinsic models, is something else.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] scale vs scale.model
parts:
some latent models will accept the 'scale' argument within f(), see the
documentation for each model

there is also a scale within inla() call, which will scale the
likelihood, see inla.doc("^gaussian$")
